headline: Nvidia has reportedly stopped making its flagship RTX 5090 gaming graphics card, according to a leaked notice from an unnamed factory.
score_reason: Curator score 7 lowered by 1: the claim rests on a leaked factory notice from an unnamed source and Nvidia has not confirmed it.
importance_line: If true, gamers and creators would face fewer and dearer top-end graphics cards while Nvidia steers its limited chip supply to costlier AI and professional products, but the claim rests on leakers and Nvidia has not confirmed it.
source: Tom's Hardware, citing leakers on X
summary: Tom's Hardware reports, citing a leaked notice from an unnamed factory shared by the X account @hongxing2020 and backed by a second leaker, that Nvidia will no longer supply the GB202 chip, the large processor inside its GeForce RTX 5090 graphics cards, leaving the RTX 5080 24GB as its top gaming card. Tom's Hardware stresses that the claim is unverified and that Nvidia has not responded; it adds that, if the report is accurate, existing stock should last for a time but fewer RTX 5090 cards would eventually reach shops and prices would be affected.
notes: Read in full via fulltext. Source is Tom's Hardware's own report of leaks posted on X. Summary keeps the hedge; Tom's Hardware's economic reasoning is its own analysis, not part of the leak.
